To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sparse-partial wavelength converters can be used to achieve excellent blocking performance in WDM networks.

the sparse-partial wavelength converter architecture can significantly reduce the number of wavelength converter and achieve excellent blocking performance, which is very close to the full-complete wavelength converter architecture.
the SPWC architecture can significantly reduce the number of wavelength conversion nodes, while achieving excellent blocking performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel network architecture that can facilitate network operators to migrate the optical network to support wavelength conversion, with minimum investment in wavelength converters.
the design of sparse-partial WDM networks, which can be considered as an alternative to full-complete wavelength conversion networks.

the following issues: 1) how to design the wavelength-routed network to save the wavelength conversion cost; 2) how to evaluate the blocking performance in wavelength-routed networks with different wavelength conversion capabilities; 3) how to evaluate blocking performance in wavelength conversion networks in the light of different wavelength converter placement strategies; 4) how to evaluate and compare the performance in wavelength-rout networks with different wavelength converter placement schemes; 5) how to evaluate wavelength conversion networks with partial wavelength conversion capability
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SPWC network architecture is an efficient and practical approach to support wavelength conversion in wavelength routed all-optical networks, which can significantly reduce the number of wavelength converter, yet maintaining excellent network performance.

, the proposed SPWC network architecture with 1%of wavelength conversion capacity is a cost-effective and practical approach for the next-generation all-optical wavelength-routed Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) network.

, with a limited number of partial wavelength conversion capability in a wavelength-routing network, one can achieve a blocking probability very close to that in the full-complete wavelength conversion case, and at the same time significantly reduce the number of wavelength conversion units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed network architecture with SPWC can be a good candidate to support the migration of optical backbone networks to wavelength conversion capability.
SPWC network architecture is a promising solution for the future all-optical networks.
, the network carriers should be able to achieve a very high blocking performance with only a very limited number of wavelength conversion capability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a small number of wavelength converters and a small number of wavelengths per fiber, we can achieve very good performance.
a sparse-partial wavelength converted network can achieve a very high performance with a small number of wavelength converters.
, in a wavelength-routing all-optical network, a small number of wavelength converters is enough to achieve excellent blocking performance, if the converters are properly placed.
